items.question: Does the CSV start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.chose: Prefixes the output with a BOM character (U+FEFF).
items.instead: Emit plain UTF-8 with no BOM.

items.question: Which line terminator ends each row, and is there a trailing one after the last row?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Use LF, and either no trailing newline or a single LF.

items.question: What columns does the CSV have, what are their header names, and in what order?
items.chose: Writes the header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created', with id, title, status, openings, filled and created date as the columns.
items.instead: Use other header labels, such as snake_case field names, or a different column set or order.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and header line only, with no data rows.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw.

items.question: In what order are the rows written?
items.chose: Sorts by creation time ascending, then by id using a UTF-16 code-unit comparison, on a copy of the input.
items.instead: Keep the input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted in the CSV?
items.chose: Writes a full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with milliseconds from toISOString().
items.instead: Write a date-only value (YYYY-MM-DD) or a locale-formatted date.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks written?
items.chose: Wraps the field in double quotes and doubles any embedded quotes (RFC 4180), only when it contains a comma, quote, CR or LF.
items.instead: Quote every field always, or also guard against spreadsheet formula injection by prefixing values that start with =, +, - or @.

items.question: What is written when a requisition has no title (missing or null)?
items.instead: Write a placeholder such as 'Untitled', or throw.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an unknown status?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id, and only the four statuses open, on_hold, filled and cancelled are allowed.
items.instead: Write the status string through unchanged, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when openings or filled is negative, fractional or non-finite?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id for any value that is not a whole number of at least 0.
items.instead: Write the number as is, clamp it, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id.
items.instead: Export the row as is, since the data is what it is, or clamp filled to openings.

items.question: What happens when one requisition in the list is invalid? Does the export fail, or does it skip that row?
items.chose: Validates every requisition before writing any output, so one bad row makes the whole build throw.
items.instead: Skip or flag the bad rows and export the rest.
